text:
alex: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands about release rhythm + oncall. I'll keep this short so we can publish a blurb.
mika: Are we standardizing on 2-week release trains or still flexible per team?
taylor: Also how do emergency hotfixes interact with the train?
alex: Target is biweekly trains for features/bug batches; teams can ship out-of-band low-risk patches if flagged. Hotfixes use an expedited path: oncall patch -> release deputy signoff (within 60m) -> canary.
ops-bot: Expedited checklist: small diff, CI smoke green, single-node canary, rollback plan, post-deploy note.
mika: Canary profile and ramp? same for Hosted and Dedicated?
alex: Default: 1% for 10m, then 10% for 10m, then 100% if healthy. Dedicated customers can request slower ramps.
taylor: What are the primary quality gates? perf/SLO thresholds?
alex: Gate = CI green, no P99 regression >10% vs baseline, <0.1% absolute 5xx increase, and successful canary.
mika: Who authorizes a pause if the canary fails?
alex: Oncall + release deputy can pause immediately; escalate to SRE lead if systemic.
taylor: Any change to oncall handover windows?
ops-bot: Handover window updated: 60m. For launch weeks, add 2h overlap day.
mika: Can we get a one-page summary and calendar of next two trains?
alex: Yes 1 I'll ask release ops to publish the summary and calendar by EOD tomorrow.
ops-bot: Reminder: add release checklist to PRs and tag oncall.
